main_content.text: What Do Our Web Development Services Include?

Good web development services cover much more than writing code. When you hire us as your web development company, the project includes everything needed to go from an idea to a live, working site, and to keep it that way.

items: Discovery: your goals, customers, competitors, services and the action you want visitors to take.
Sitemap and content plan: which pages you need, what each should say and which search terms each page should own.
Wireframes and visual design: layout for desktop and mobile, brand colours, type and imagery.
Development: theme or front-end build, CMS set-up, forms, integrations and performance work.
Content entry: your text, images and documents placed, formatted and checked.
SEO foundations: titles, descriptions, headings, clean URLs, XML sitemap, redirects and structured data.
Tracking: Google Analytics, Search Console and conversion tracking for calls, forms and WhatsApp clicks.
Testing: real phones and browsers, forms, speed, accessibility checks and broken links.
Launch and handover: DNS, SSL, backups, a training session and a written guide for your team.

main_content.text: Website Design Services vs Website Development

People often use the two terms as if they mean the same thing, but they are different stages. Our website design services decide how the site looks and how a visitor moves through it. Development turns that design into a working site that loads fast, can be edited and connects to your other tools. We do both, which is why we describe our offer as web design development services rather than one or the other.

rows: Layout, look, navigation, page structure, calls to action
Code, CMS, forms, speed, security, integrations
Text, images, proof and offers on each page

main_content.text: What Should Professional Web Design Services Deliver?

"Professional" should mean more than a nice look. Professional web design services deliver a site that matches your brand, works on small screens first, uses readable type and contrast, and puts the most important information where visitors expect it. Each page should have one clear purpose and one main action. If a design looks impressive but makes it harder to find your phone number, it is not professional design.
Which Platform Is Right: WordPress, Drupal or a Custom Build?

There is no single best platform, and a web development company that recommends the same one to everyone is not listening. The right choice depends on who will edit the site, how complex it is, what it must connect to and how much you want to spend on upkeep. We recommend a platform only after discovery, and we explain why.

Huge ecosystem, easy editing, many developers available
Needs regular updates; too many plugins slow it down

Fast front end, content reused across platforms

main_content.text: WordPress is by far the most widely used content management system. W3Techs data reported in 2026 puts it at roughly four in ten of all websites. That popularity is a strength, because themes, plugins and help are easy to find, and a risk, because poorly maintained WordPress sites are common targets for attackers.
WordPress Development Services

Our WordPress development services cover new builds, theme development, block-editor (Gutenberg) layouts, plugin selection, speed work and migrations. As a WordPress development company we keep plugins to the minimum the site truly needs, use licensed themes or build our own, and set user roles so your team can edit content without breaking the layout.

Our WordPress website development services are a good fit for most companies that want to update pages, publish news or blogs and add landing pages without calling a developer. If you need a WordPress developer for a specific job, such as fixing a broken theme or speeding up a slow site, we take on those smaller tasks too.
A WordPress Website Design Agency That Also Writes the Code

Many studios design in a page builder and stop there. As a WordPress website design agency with in-house developers, we design each template for the block editor and build it cleanly, so pages stay fast and consistent as your team adds content over the years.
Drupal Website Development Services

Our Drupal website development services suit organisations with complex content: many departments, user roles, approval workflows or languages. We build on supported Drupal versions and help teams move off old ones. Drupal 7 reached its end of life on 5 January 2025, which means the Drupal Security Team no longer provides fixes for it. If your site still runs Drupal 7, planning a migration is the safest next step.
CMS Web Development Services and Headless Builds

Our CMS web development services go beyond WordPress and Drupal. For some projects we use a headless CMS, where editors manage content in one place and a fast custom front end displays it. This works well when content must also appear in a mobile app or on several sites. We only suggest it when the benefits clearly outweigh the extra build effort.
When a Fully Custom Build Makes Sense

If your site is really an application, with logins, dashboards, bookings, calculations or deep integrations, a custom build is usually better than forcing a CMS to do the job. That work is handled by our custom web development team.

Corporate website development has extra needs. Several teams contribute content, legal and leadership approve pages, and the site often has sections for investors, media, careers and policies. We set up roles and approval steps in the CMS, create templates for each section, and document how the site should be updated so it stays consistent long after launch.

main_content.text: How We Protect Rankings During a Redesign

A redesign is the most common way businesses lose search traffic. Before launch, we crawl the old site, map every old URL to its new home, keep titles and content that already rank, and set up 301 redirects. After launch, we watch Search Console for errors and fix anything that slips through.

main_content.text: What Standards Does Every Website We Build Meet?

We build every site to the same baseline, whatever the platform. These are targets we design and test for, not guarantees, because real-world results also depend on hosting, content and plugins you add later.
Speed and Core Web Vitals
Google's Core Web Vitals measure how real visitors experience a page. We aim for the "good" range on each metric and check field data in Search Console after launch.

rows: How quickly the main content appears
How quickly the page responds to taps and clicks
How much the layout jumps while loading

main_content.text: Mobile First

Google announced in 2024 that it was completing its move to mobile-first indexing, which means it mainly uses the mobile version of a site for indexing and ranking. We design the mobile layout first and make sure the mobile and desktop versions carry the same content.
Accessibility

We follow the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, which became a W3C Recommendation on 6 October 2023 and added nine new success criteria. In practice that means readable contrast, keyboard access, clear focus states, labelled forms, alt text and tap targets large enough for thumbs. We do automated and manual checks, but we do not issue legal accessibility certificates.
Security and Reliability

items: HTTPS on every page, with automatic certificate renewal where the host supports it.
Supported platform versions, licensed themes and plugins, and no pirated or "nulled" software.
Strong admin passwords, two-step login for admins and limited user roles.
Automated off-site backups and a tested restore process when you take a care plan.
Contact forms protected from spam without blocking real users.

Structured data that matches what is visible on the page.
Server-rendered content, so search engines and AI tools can read it without running scripts.
Internal links between related pages, and 301 redirects for any URL that changes.

Uptime monitoring and security scans, with alerts handled by our team.
Small content edits, new pages from existing templates and image updates.
A short monthly report: what was updated, any issues found and suggested improvements.
Speed and Core Web Vitals checks after major changes.

Three Typical Situations We Help With
These situations are illustrative. They are based on common requests; names and details are changed, and they are not client case studies or promised results.
Situation 1: A Consultancy With a Site Nobody Can Edit

A small accounting consultancy (details changed) has a site built in a heavy page builder by a freelancer who no longer replies. Every text change breaks the layout. We would rebuild it on WordPress with block-editor templates for services, team and articles, move the existing content, redirect old URLs and train two staff members to edit pages safely.
Situation 2: An Institute Still Running Drupal 7

A training institute (details changed) runs a large Drupal 7 site with courses, faculty profiles and an admissions section. With Drupal 7 no longer supported, the site is a security risk. We would audit the content types and modules, plan a migration to a supported Drupal version or another suitable platform, move content in stages and redirect every old course URL.
Situation 3: A Manufacturer Moving From Brochure to Enquiries

A component manufacturer (details changed) has a five-page site with no product information. Buyers call to ask basic questions. We would plan product category pages with specifications and downloadable data sheets, add a request-a-quote form, set up conversion tracking and structure the pages so they can rank for the products buyers actually search for.
Common Mistakes When Building or Redesigning a Website
These mistakes cost businesses time, money and search traffic. Most are easy to avoid if you know about them early.

items: Registering the domain or hosting in the developer's name instead of your own.
Choosing a theme for its demo pictures, then finding it slow and hard to edit with real content.
Installing dozens of plugins for small features that could be built simply or skipped.
Launching a redesign without redirecting old URLs, losing years of rankings overnight.
Writing content after the design is finished, so the text never fits the layout.
Using pirated themes or plugins, which often contain hidden malware.
Testing only on a desktop when most visitors arrive on phones.
Forgetting tracking, so nobody knows which pages produce enquiries.
Having no update or backup plan after launch.

Choosing a web development company is less about finding the cheapest quote and more about finding a team that understands what your site must achieve. A useful way to compare providers is to look at four things: how they plan, how they build, how they hand over and how they support you after launch.

main_content.text: A web development company that also understands search and conversion will usually save you money over the life of the site, because pages are structured to rank and to turn visitors into enquiries from day one. That is the gap we try to close: our developers, designers and SEO specialists work as one team, so you do not pay one web development company to build and another agency to fix what was built.
Responsive Website Design as a Basic Requirement

A responsive website adapts its layout to any screen, from a small phone to a wide monitor. Today this is not an extra; it is the minimum. We design responsive layouts with flexible grids, images sized for each screen, readable text without zooming and buttons large enough to tap. We then test each template on real phones and tablets, not just a desktop browser window.
Website Design Solutions for Different Budgets

Every business has limits on time and money, so we offer website design solutions at different levels of depth. A small business may start with a carefully adapted theme and a handful of strong pages; a larger company may need a custom design system with dozens of templates. In both cases, the web development company you hire should be able to explain what you get at each level and what you would give up.
Questions to Ask Before You Hire a Web Development Company
Ask any provider these questions, including us. A good partner will answer clearly and in writing.

items: Which platform do you recommend for my site, and why that one?
Will the domain, hosting, code and design files be in my name from day one?
How many plugins or third-party tools will the site use, and who maintains them?
How will you protect my current rankings if this is a redesign?
What speed and accessibility checks do you run before launch?
How many rounds of design changes are included?
Who will be my main contact, and how often will I get updates?
What happens after launch if something breaks?

Copy a competitor's design or content, or use images and fonts you do not have the right to use.
Use pirated, cracked or "nulled" themes and plugins.
Cover full online stores; those are handled by our e-commerce development service.
Cover complex web applications; those are handled by our custom web development service.
Include ongoing SEO campaigns or paid ads, which are separate services.
Provide legal advice or certify legal compliance for privacy, accessibility or industry rules.
Lock you in. We never keep your domain, code or content hostage.

main_content.text: When You Do Not Need Us
We would rather tell you honestly when a full website project is not the right spend.

items: If you need a one-page site for a short event, a hosted website builder is quicker and cheaper.
If your current site is fast, secure and converts well, better content and SEO may help more than a redesign.
If you only need a small fix, such as a broken form, ask for a one-off task instead of a new build.
If you have an in-house developer, a design-only engagement or an audit may be all you need.
If you are not yet sure what you sell or to whom, talk to customers before investing in a site.

main_content.text: Special Cases and Edge Cases
Some projects need extra care. We plan for these separately.
Hacked or Infected Websites

If your site shows spam pages, redirects visitors or is flagged as unsafe, we first take a backup for evidence, clean the infection, close the hole that let it in, update everything and request a review in Search Console where needed. Then we decide together whether a rebuild is safer.
Moving From a Website Builder

Moving from a hosted builder to WordPress or another CMS means exporting content, rebuilding templates and redirecting URLs. Some builders limit exports, so we check what can be moved automatically before quoting.
Indian-Language and Multilingual Sites
For sites in Hindi, Kannada, Tamil or other languages, we choose fonts that render well, plan translated URLs, add hreflang tags and make sure forms accept non-English input.
Sites With Specific Compliance Needs

If your site must follow rules set by a regulator, a funding body or a government department, tell us at the start. We confirm the current requirements with you and your adviser before design begins, rather than assuming what applies.
Very Large Content Migrations
For sites with thousands of pages, we migrate in batches with scripts, check samples by hand and keep the old site available on a staging address until every redirect is confirmed.

main_content.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Our Web Development Company
What does a web development company do?

A web development company plans, designs, builds, tests and launches websites, and often maintains them afterwards. It turns your goals and content into a fast, secure site that visitors can use and search engines can read.
What is included in your website development services?

Our website development services include discovery, sitemap and content planning, design, development, content entry, basic on-page SEO, tracking, testing, launch and training. Care plans for updates and backups are optional.
Do you build websites on WordPress?
Yes. WordPress is our most common choice for business and content sites because it is easy to edit and widely supported. We keep plugins to a minimum and use licensed themes or our own.
Are you a WordPress development company or do you use other platforms too?
We are a WordPress development company, and we also build on Drupal, headless CMS set-ups and custom code. We recommend a platform after discovery, based on your content, editors and integrations.
Do you offer Drupal website development services?
Yes. Drupal suits large, structured sites with many content types, roles or languages. We also help organisations migrate from Drupal 7, which reached end of life on 5 January 2025.
What are CMS web development services?

Do you offer website redesign services?
Yes. We start with an audit to decide whether repair or rebuild is better value, then redesign the site with redirects and checks that protect your existing search rankings.
Will a new website or redesign affect my Google rankings?
A poorly handled redesign can lose rankings. We map every old URL, keep content that already ranks, set up 301 redirects and monitor Search Console after launch to reduce that risk.
Do you offer WordPress website management services after launch?
Yes. Our care plans cover updates, backups, uptime and security monitoring, small edits and a short monthly report. You can stop at any time.
Do you build corporate websites?
Yes. Our corporate website development includes sections for services, news, careers, investors or policies, with user roles and approval steps so several teams can contribute safely.
Will I own my website?
Yes. The domain, hosting account, code, design files and content are yours, and we can work entirely inside accounts registered in your name.
Will my website work well on mobile phones?
Yes. We design the mobile layout first, test on real phones and aim for Google's "good" Core Web Vitals thresholds for loading, responsiveness and layout stability.
Are you one of the top web development companies in India?
We do not claim a rank, and we suggest caution with "top" lists because some are paid. Judge any provider by real work, references and how clearly it explains its plan.
How long does it take to build a website?
It depends on the number of pages and features, content readiness and feedback speed. We give you an indicative schedule by stage in the written proposal.
How much does website development cost?
The total depends on pages, features, design depth, content, integrations, migration and third-party costs. Our team shares the exact total after reviewing your requirements.
Do you work with clients outside Bengaluru?
Yes. We have one office in Whitefield, Bengaluru, and we work with clients across India and abroad through video calls, project boards and a review site.

main_content.text: What Is Custom Web Development, and How Is It Different From a Website?

A website mainly publishes information: services, contact details, articles. A web application does work. People log in, enter data, follow steps, get results and see reports. Custom web development is the craft of building those applications for one organisation's needs, rather than adapting a general product made for thousands of customers.

rows: Company site with services and a contact form
A web design and development team
Lets users log in and complete tasks
Gives a group of users their own secure area
Customer, dealer, vendor or student portal
General tool rented by many businesses

main_content.text: If what you need is a marketing website, our website development team is the right fit. If people need to log in and get work done, you are in the territory of custom software.
Build, Buy or Extend: When Is Custom Software the Right Choice?

Custom software is not always the answer, and an honest software development company should say so. Many good products already exist. The question is whether one of them fits closely enough, and what it will cost to live with the gaps.

rows: A standard tool covers most of your needs and your process is common

Your current tool is mostly right but lacks a few features or connections

Your process is a competitive advantage, or no product fits without heavy workarounds

Off-the-shelf for standard needs, custom for the parts that make you different

main_content.text: A Quick Decision Checklist

items: Do your teams copy the same data between two or more tools every day?
Do you pay for many user licences mainly so people can view a few reports?
Is a key step in your process handled in spreadsheets because no tool supports it?
Would a mistake in that manual step cost you a customer, money or compliance trouble?
Is the way you work part of why customers choose you?

main_content.text: If you answered yes to two or more, custom software deserves a serious look. If not, improving or connecting your current tools may be enough, and we will tell you that.
What Do Our Software Development Services Include?

Our software development services cover the full life of an application, from the first workshop to support after launch. You can hire us for the whole journey or for one part, such as specification, front-end work or an integration.

items: Discovery workshops to map users, roles, steps, data and pain points.

UX and interface design, tested with real users where possible.
Front-end and back-end development in short, reviewable cycles.
Database design, data migration and reporting.
Integrations with payment gateways, accounting, messaging, maps and other systems.
Automated and manual testing, security checks and performance testing.
Deployment, monitoring, backups and documentation.
Training, handover and optional ongoing support.

main_content.text: Web Application Development Services

Our web application development services turn a business process into software people can use from any browser. Typical examples include quoting and order tools, approval workflows, inventory and dispatch systems, booking engines and reporting dashboards. We sometimes describe these as web app development services because many clients search that way; the meaning is the same.
Web Portal Development Company for Customers, Partners and Teams

As a web portal development company, we build secure areas where a specific group of people can log in and see only what belongs to them: customers checking orders and invoices, dealers placing orders, vendors uploading documents, students accessing courses, or employees submitting requests. Role-based access, audit trails and clear dashboards are standard.
Custom CRM Development

Many businesses outgrow generic CRMs, or pay for features they never use while missing the one they need. As a CRM development company, we build lean CRMs around your sales stages, lead sources and follow-up rules, connected to your website forms, phone system, WhatsApp and email where the providers allow it.
Custom ERP Development

Custom ERP development rarely means replacing everything at once. We usually build the modules that standard ERPs handle badly for your business, such as production planning, job costing, field service or multi-location stock, and connect them to the accounting or ERP system you already use.
Back-End Development and Integrations

As a backend development company, we build the databases, APIs, background jobs and integrations that make applications reliable. We document every API so your team or other vendors can build on it later.
Front End Development Services

Our front end development services focus on interfaces that are fast, accessible and easy to learn. We build reusable components, keep forms short, show clear error messages and test on the devices your users actually have.
Features We Often Build Into a Custom Web Application
Every custom web application is different, but some building blocks come up again and again. Planning them early saves time later:

items: Secure login with roles, permissions and optional two-step verification.
Dashboards with filters, charts and exports to Excel or PDF.
Multi-step forms with validation, file uploads and saved drafts.
Approval workflows with notifications by email, SMS or WhatsApp.
Search across records, with saved views for different teams.
Audit trails that show who changed what, and when.
Scheduled reports and automatic reminders.
An admin area to manage users, settings and master data without a developer.

main_content.text: API Integration: How We Connect Your Systems

Most of the value in custom software comes from connecting it to the tools you already rely on. API integration means two systems exchange data automatically through a documented interface, so nobody has to re-type information. As a full stack team, we commonly connect applications to payment gateways, accounting software, email and SMS services, WhatsApp Business messaging, maps and location services, e-signature tools and existing ERPs or CRMs.

Before we promise an integration, we check four things: whether the other system offers an API, what it costs to use, what limits apply to requests and data, and whether a sandbox is available for testing. When no API exists, we look at safer alternatives such as scheduled file exports and imports. Every integration we build includes error handling and alerts, so a failed sync is noticed and fixed instead of silently losing data.
Which Technology Stack Do We Use?
We choose the stack after discovery, based on what the application must do, who will maintain it and where it will run. We do not force one framework on every project.

Laravel Development Company

Our MERN stack development services suit products where speed of change matters and the data model is flexible. If your existing team or system uses Angular, a MEAN stack developer from our team can work within that set-up instead of forcing a rewrite.

As a travel software development company, we build booking and quoting tools for agencies, tour operators and travel startups. Supplier and global distribution system connections need commercial agreements and certification from those providers, so we plan them with you from the start rather than promising them on day one.
Enterprise Software Development Company Work

For larger organisations, we work as an enterprise software development company on defined workstreams: a new internal platform, a module that sits beside an existing ERP, or a modern front end for a legacy system. We follow your security reviews, access rules and release processes. The same applies when we act as an enterprise app development company for internal web apps used by many departments.
How Does Our Custom Software Development Process Work?
We work in short cycles so you see progress early and can change direction before it becomes expensive.

items: Discovery workshop with the people who will use and approve the software.
Written specification: users, roles, screens, data, integrations and acceptance criteria.
Proposal with scope, phases, team and the exact total for the first phase.
Clickable prototype of key screens, tested with a few real users.
Development in two-week sprints, each ending with a demo on a test server.
Testing: automated tests, manual checks, security review and load testing where needed.
Data migration, training and launch, often to a small group first.
Support, monitoring and a plan for the next set of features.

main_content.text: How Do We Handle Changes in Scope?

New ideas always appear once people see working software, and that is a good thing. We handle them openly. Each new request is written down, estimated and placed in a backlog. You then decide whether it replaces something in the current phase, waits for the next one or is added with a written change to the total. Nothing is added silently, and nothing you approved is dropped without your agreement. This keeps the budget predictable while leaving room to improve the product as you learn.
How Do We Test Custom Software?
Testing runs through every sprint, not just the final week. Each feature is checked against the acceptance criteria written in the specification before it is shown to you.

items: Automated unit and integration tests for business rules, calculations and APIs.
End-to-end tests for the most important user journeys, such as login, ordering and approvals.
Manual testing on the browsers and devices your users actually have.
Role testing, to confirm each type of user sees only what they should.
Security checks against the OWASP Top 10 and a review of third-party packages.
Performance tests with realistic data before launch.
User acceptance testing by your team on a test server, with issues tracked until closed.

main_content.text: How Do We Keep Your Application Secure?

Security is designed in, not added at the end. We use the OWASP Top 10, the widely used list of the most critical web application security risks, as a baseline checklist. The 2025 edition puts Broken Access Control first, followed by Security Misconfiguration and Software Supply Chain Failures.

items: Role-based access checked on the server for every request, not only hidden in the interface.
Secure defaults: least-privilege accounts, secrets kept out of code, regular dependency updates.
Encrypted connections, strong password storage and optional two-step login.
Input validation and parameterised queries to prevent injection.
Logging and alerting for important actions, with clocks synchronised for accurate records.
Backups with tested restores, and separate test and live environments.

main_content.text: Indian Rules That May Apply to Your System

Some rules depend on who you are and what data you hold. CERT-In's directions of 28 April 2022 require covered entities to report specified cyber incidents within six hours and keep system logs for a rolling 180 days within India. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 are coming into force in phases. We can build the logging, consent and access features these rules need, but your legal adviser should confirm which obligations apply to your business.
How Do We Plan for Performance and Growth?

An application that works for ten users can struggle with a thousand. We plan for the load you expect over the next few years, not just launch day. That means indexing databases around real queries, caching data that rarely changes, moving slow work such as report generation into background jobs, and choosing hosting that can scale up when needed.

Before launch, we test with realistic data volumes and, where the use case calls for it, simulated traffic. We set targets with you in the specification, for example how quickly a dashboard should load with a year of data, and we measure against them. We do not quote headline numbers that were not tested on your system.
Who Owns the Code? IP, Documentation and Handover

You do. Our standard agreement assigns ownership of the custom code we write for you, and we work in repositories and cloud accounts registered to your company wherever possible. Open-source libraries keep their own licences, which we list for you.

items: Source code in your Git repository, with a clear history of changes.
Technical documentation: architecture, set-up steps, environment variables and deployment.
API documentation for every endpoint we build.
An admin guide and short training videos for your team.
A handover session if you move support in-house or to another vendor.

main_content.text: What Does the Total Cost Depend On?
We do not publish fixed prices on this page, because two applications that sound similar can need very different work. The total is made up of a few clear parts:

items: Number of user roles, screens and workflows.
Complexity of business rules, calculations and approvals.
Integrations, and whether third-party APIs are well documented.
Data migration from spreadsheets or old systems.
Security, audit and performance requirements.
Design depth, from a clean standard interface to a fully custom design system.
Third-party costs such as cloud hosting, paid APIs, SMS or email services, paid directly to those providers.
Ongoing support and new features after launch.

main_content.text: Our team shares the exact total after reviewing your requirements, usually phase by phase, so you can start with the most valuable part.
Three Typical Situations We Help With
These situations are illustrative. They are based on common requests; names and details are changed, and they are not client case studies or promised results.
Situation 1: A Distributor Running on Spreadsheets

A building-materials distributor (details changed) takes dealer orders by phone and WhatsApp, then re-types them into spreadsheets and accounting software. Errors and delays are common. We would build a dealer portal for orders and stock visibility, an internal dispatch screen and an integration with their accounting software, then move dealers onto it in groups.
Situation 2: A Travel Agency Quoting by Hand

A tour operator (details changed) builds every quotation manually from supplier rates kept in emails. Quotes take hours and pricing mistakes slip through. We would build a quoting tool with a rate library, margin rules, branded PDF quotes and a simple booking tracker, leaving supplier API connections for a later phase once agreements are in place.
Situation 3: An Institute Outgrowing Its CRM

A coaching institute (details changed) pays for a large CRM but uses only a fraction of it, while fee tracking and batch scheduling live in spreadsheets. We would build a lean CRM for enquiries and follow-ups, with admissions, fee schedules and batch allocation in one place, and export their history from the old tool.
What Makes Custom Software Succeed After Launch?
The best code still fails if people do not use it. Adoption is part of the project, not an afterthought, and a good software development company plans for it from the first workshop.

items: Involve the people who will use the software in discovery and in testing the prototype.
Launch to a small group first, fix what they find, then roll out to everyone.
Replace the old process on a clear date, so people do not keep two systems running.
Give each team a short guide and a named person to ask for help.
Measure what matters: time saved, errors reduced, faster responses to customers.
Review usage after the first month and plan improvements based on real feedback.

main_content.text: When these steps are skipped, teams quietly return to spreadsheets and the investment is wasted. When they are followed, the software becomes part of how the business runs.
Common Mistakes With Custom Software Projects
Most failed software projects fail for reasons that have little to do with code. These are the ones we see most often.

items: Starting development without a written specification that users and managers have approved.
Trying to build every feature in version one instead of launching the most valuable part first.
Leaving the people who will use the software out of discovery and testing.
Letting the vendor host the code and data in their own accounts.
Underestimating data migration, especially from messy spreadsheets.
Skipping automated tests to save time, then paying for it in every later release.
Having no budget or plan for support after launch.
Choosing a framework because it is fashionable rather than because it fits the team that will maintain it.

main_content.text: Questions to Ask a Software Development Company Before You Sign
Ask these of any provider, including us. Clear answers in writing are a good sign.

items: Who will work on my project, and will the same people stay until launch?
How will you document requirements, and how do we handle changes in scope?
How often will I see working software, not just status updates?
Where will the code, database and cloud accounts live, and in whose name?
How do you test, and what security checks do you run before launch?
What happens if a key developer leaves your team?
What support do you offer after launch, and how fast do you respond to serious issues?
Can I speak to a past client, and can you show similar work with permission?

main_content.text: Questions to Ask Your Current Software Vendors
Integrations depend on other people's systems. Before the project starts, ask your existing vendors:

items: Do you provide an API, and is it included in our plan or charged separately?
Are there limits on how many requests we can make or how much data we can export?
Can we get a test or sandbox account for development?
Who in your team can answer technical questions during the integration?

main_content.text: What This Service Does Not Do
To keep expectations clear, our custom web development service does not:

items: Promise a fixed delivery date before the specification is agreed.
Sell you a ready-made product and call it custom.
Keep your code, data or cloud accounts in our name.
Build features designed to collect personal data without proper notice and consent.
Provide legal, tax or regulatory advice; we build to the requirements your advisers confirm.
Cover marketing websites, online stores or native mobile apps, which have their own pages and teams.
Use cracked or unlicensed software, libraries or tools.

main_content.text: When You Do Not Need Custom Software
We would rather save you money than sell you a build you do not need.

items: If a well-known product fits most of your process and the gaps are small, configure it instead.
If the main problem is that tools do not talk to each other, a few integrations may solve it.
If you are still testing whether customers want the idea, a no-code prototype may be enough for now.
If your team will not change how it works, new software will not fix the problem on its own.
If there is no budget for support after launch, wait until there is.

main_content.text: Special Cases and Edge Cases
Some projects need extra planning. These are the ones we treat separately.
Taking Over Code Built by Someone Else

If your previous developer has left, we start with a code and infrastructure audit: what exists, what is documented, what is risky and what can be kept. Only then do we suggest whether to continue, refactor or rebuild parts of it.
Replacing a Legacy System

Old systems often hold years of business rules nobody has written down. We document those rules first, run old and new systems in parallel where possible, and migrate users in stages to avoid a risky single switch-over.
Messy Data Migration
Spreadsheets with duplicate customers, inconsistent dates and free-text fields are normal. We clean and map the data with scripts, show you samples to approve and keep the original files untouched.
Multi-Tenant or SaaS Products

If you plan to sell your software to other businesses, the architecture changes: separate data for each customer, subscription billing and self-service onboarding. We plan for this from the first specification.
Low-Connectivity Users
Field staff and rural users may work on weak networks. We keep pages light, save drafts locally and sync when the connection returns, so work is not lost.
Support and Improvements After Launch

Software keeps changing after launch, as users suggest improvements and the business grows. Our optional support covers bug fixes, security and dependency updates, monitoring, backups and small enhancements, with response times agreed in writing. Larger features are planned and quoted as new phases. You can end support at any time and receive a full handover.
Response Times and Service Levels

Support terms are agreed in writing before launch, not assumed. We classify issues by impact: a critical problem stops the business from working, a major one blocks a team or feature, and a minor one is an inconvenience with a workaround. Each level has its own response and resolution target, matched to the support plan you choose and to what your hosting provider can offer. We do not quote uptime percentages that depend on infrastructure we do not control; instead, we set up monitoring so that both you and our team see the same numbers.
Custom Software Development Company in India: How We Work With Clients

Afwan Tech has one office, in Whitefield, Bengaluru, and no branch offices elsewhere. We work with clients across India and abroad through workshops on video calls, shared project boards, sprint demos on a test server and a single point of contact. When it helps, we hold discovery workshops in person in Bengaluru.

If you are comparing several options for a custom software development company, look at how clearly each one explains its process, ownership terms and support plan. A software development company that answers those questions well before the contract is usually easier to work with after it.

We would rather earn trust through how we work than through badges. Here is what you can expect from us as your software development company:

items: Honest build-versus-buy advice before any code is written.
A written specification and an exact total for each phase.

main_content.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Our Software Development Company
What does a software development company do?

A software development company plans, designs, builds, tests and supports software. For custom web projects, that means turning your processes into web applications, portals and tools your team and customers use in a browser.
What is custom web development?

bottom_content.text: Custom Web Development From a Software Development Company That Shows Its Work

**Afwan Tech** is a Bengaluru team, based in Whitefield, that builds custom web applications, portals and business systems around the way your organisation actually works. Building your own system is the right choice when off-the-shelf tools force your team into workarounds, spreadsheets and repeated data entry. We start by mapping your process, then recommend whether to buy, extend or build, and we say so plainly when custom software is not the best use of your budget.

Our software development services cover discovery, written specifications, interface design, front-end and back-end work, integrations, testing, deployment, documentation and support. As a custom software development company, we focus on the parts of your operation that make you different, and our custom software development services are delivered in short sprints, so you review working software every two weeks instead of waiting months for a reveal.

Our web application development services turn processes such as quoting, ordering, approvals, dispatch and reporting into secure browser-based tools. Some clients call these web app development services; either way, the goal is fewer manual steps and fewer errors. As a web portal development company, we build customer, dealer, vendor, student and employee portals where each user sees only what belongs to them.

Many businesses ask us for tools that generic products handle poorly. As a CRM development company, we build lean CRMs around your sales stages and follow-up rules. Our custom ERP development work adds modules for production, job costing, field service or stock beside the accounting or ERP system you already use. As a travel software development company, we build quoting tools, booking engines and agent portals, planning supplier connections around each provider's approval.

On the technical side, we work as a React development company for complex interfaces, a Laravel development company for PHP projects and a backend development company for APIs, databases and background jobs. Our front end development services focus on fast, accessible screens, and our MERN stack development services suit products that change quickly. If your existing system is built on Angular, a MEAN stack developer from our team can work within it.

For larger organisations, we act as an enterprise software development company on clearly defined workstreams, following your security reviews and release processes, and as an enterprise app development company for internal tools used across departments. Security follows the OWASP Top 10, with role-based access enforced on the server, updated dependencies and logged actions.

How a project runs is simple. A discovery workshop maps users, roles, steps and data. A written specification lists screens, rules and acceptance criteria, and a proposal sets out the phases and the exact total for the first one. A clickable prototype is tested with a few real users before the build starts. During the build you see a demo every two weeks on a test server, and new ideas go into a backlog that you prioritise. Before launch we run automated tests, manual checks, role testing and security reviews, migrate your data and train your team.

Most of the value comes from connecting systems. Every API integration we build, whether with payment gateways, accounting software, messaging services or an existing ERP, includes error handling and alerts so a failed sync never goes unnoticed. As a full stack team, we design each custom web application so that its data, screens and integrations can grow with the business.

Custom software is not always the answer. If a well-known product covers most of your process, configuring it is usually cheaper. If your tools simply do not talk to each other, a few integrations may be enough. If you are still testing an idea, a quick no-code prototype can prove demand first. We will tell you which of these fits before any code is written, because the right advice now builds a longer working relationship than an unnecessary project.

You own the code, database, documentation and cloud accounts. We do not promise fixed dates before a specification is agreed, and we do not quote uptime or speed figures we have not tested on your system. Pricing for each phase is shared after we review your requirements.

Shopify, Magento and custom e-commerce stores designed, built and grown by one team in Bengaluru.

main_content.text: What Does a Shopify Developer Do?

A Shopify developer turns a standard Shopify account into a store that fits your brand, products and operations. The work ranges from small theme changes to custom apps that connect Shopify with other systems. When you hire us, your Shopify developer handles:

items: Theme set-up and customisation, including sections and templates your team can edit.
Custom page and product layouts written in Liquid, Shopify's template language.
Product structure: variants, collections, filters, metafields and bundles.
Checkout settings, payment providers, shipping rules and tax configuration.
App selection, so you install only what you need, and custom apps where no good app exists.
Integrations with ERP, accounting, warehouse, courier and marketing tools.
Speed work: image sizes, script clean-up and removing apps that slow pages down.
Data migration from another platform, with redirects for old product URLs.

main_content.text: Shopify Web Development vs Shopify Web Design

Shopify web design decides how the store looks and how shoppers move from a product to checkout. Shopify web development makes that design work: templates, features, integrations and speed. As a Shopify web design agency with in-house developers, we do both, so the design you approve is built faithfully and stays fast as you add products.
Shopify Website Development Services

Our Shopify website development services cover new stores, redesigns of existing stores and moves from other platforms. As a Shopify website development company, we start with your catalogue and operations, not with a theme demo, because a store that looks good but cannot handle your variants, stock or delivery rules creates work every day.
Shopify App Development Company Work

Sometimes no app in the Shopify App Store does exactly what you need, or the available apps charge high monthly fees for one small feature. As a Shopify app development company, we build custom apps for a single store: special pricing rules, B2B ordering, ERP sync, custom reports or loyalty logic. Custom apps stay private to your store and are documented so another Shopify developer could maintain them later.
Shopify Dev Stores, Development Stores and Client Transfer Stores

People often ask about a Shopify development store. Shopify Partners use development stores to build and test apps and themes, and according to Shopify's Partner documentation, development stores cannot be transferred to a client. When a store is being built for a merchant, the Partner creates a client transfer store instead and hands ownership to the merchant when it is ready to go live. We follow that route, or we work directly inside a store you have created, so ownership is clear from the start. Many teams simply call all of these "Shopify dev stores", but the difference matters at handover, and an experienced Shopify developer will explain which one is being used for your project.
When Should You Hire a Shopify Developer?

Shopify is designed so that merchants can start without code, and many small stores never need a developer. You should consider hiring a Shopify developer when the store starts holding the business back. Common signs include:

items: Your theme cannot show your products the way customers need, such as size charts, bundles or comparison tables.
You pay for several apps that each do one small thing, and the store has slowed down.
Staff copy orders, stock or invoices between Shopify and other systems by hand.
You need B2B prices, customer-specific catalogues or quote requests.
You are moving from another platform and cannot risk losing products, customers or rankings.
Checkout, shipping or tax rules need changes you cannot make in the settings alone.

main_content.text: In these cases, a Shopify developer usually saves more in time, app fees and lost sales than the project costs. If none of these apply, a well-chosen theme and careful settings may be all you need for now.
Shopify Developer vs Freelancer vs In-House Team
There are three common ways to get Shopify work done. Each suits a different stage of business.

Make sure one named person owns your project
You have a small, clearly defined task
Availability, holidays and handover if they move on
Your store is large and changes every week
Salary, tools and keeping skills current

main_content.text: Whichever route you choose, insist that the store, apps and code stay in your business's accounts, so changing your Shopify developer later is simple.
Which Platform Fits Your Store: Shopify, Magento, WooCommerce or Custom?

There is no single best e-commerce platform. The right one depends on your catalogue, order volume, team, integrations and budget for running costs. We recommend a platform after discovery and explain the trade-offs in writing.

rows: Most D2C brands and growing stores
Hosted, secure, quick to launch, large app ecosystem
Monthly fees and app costs; some checkout limits outside higher plans

Very flexible, strong catalogue and pricing rules
Needs hosting, skilled developers and regular upgrades
Performance and security depend on hosting and upkeep
Unusual workflows, very high performance needs, multi-channel content
Full control over front end and logic
Highest build effort; needs a long-term technical partner

main_content.text: Magento Website Development

Our Magento website development work suits retailers and distributors with large catalogues, many customer groups, tiered pricing or several store views. Magento ecommerce development services include new builds, extension development, upgrades, performance tuning and integrations with ERP and warehouse systems. If you need a Magento developer for a specific job, such as fixing a checkout error or applying security patches, we take on focused tasks too.

Magento 1 reached its end of life on 30 June 2020, and Adobe stopped releasing security fixes for it. Stores still running Magento 1 carry a growing security and payment-compliance risk; moving to Magento 2 or another platform is the safer path.
Headless and Custom Ecommerce Web Development

In a headless store, the shopping engine (for example Shopify or Magento) manages products, carts and orders, while a separate custom front end shows them. This can give very fast pages and lets the same product data feed a website, an app and other channels. It costs more to build and maintain, so we suggest headless ecommerce web development only when the benefits are clear for your business.
What Do Our Ecommerce Solutions Include?
Our ecommerce solutions cover everything needed to launch and run a store, not just the pages shoppers see.

rows: Categories, collections, variants, filters, product templates, bulk product import
Home, category, product, cart and content pages designed mobile-first

main_content.text: B2B and Wholesale Stores

Wholesale buyers need different things from retail shoppers: customer-specific prices, minimum order quantities, quick re-ordering, credit terms and GST invoices. We build B2B stores and portals that handle these rules, either on the store platform itself or with a custom layer connected to it.
Payments, Shipping and Tax for Indian Online Stores
Selling in India comes with its own set-up work. We configure these parts with your providers and advisers.

items: Payments: we connect payment gateways that work with your platform and business type, including UPI, cards, net banking and wallets. Each gateway has its own approval process and fees, agreed directly between you and the provider.

Saved cards: under RBI rules in force since October 2022, merchants in India cannot store customers' actual card numbers; saved-card checkout works through tokens issued via the card networks and banks. Reputable gateways handle this for you, and we never store card data in your store.
Cash on delivery: we set rules for which products, pin codes or order values allow it, to reduce failed deliveries.
Shipping: we integrate couriers or shipping aggregators for rates, labels, pickups and tracking, and configure serviceable pin codes.
Tax and invoices: we set up tax rates and invoice formats as your chartered accountant advises; we do not give tax advice.

main_content.text: What Must an Indian Online Store Show Customers?

The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 set duties for e-commerce businesses selling to consumers in India. Among other things, they require clear business and contact details, a named grievance officer whose contact details are shown on the site, and complaints acknowledged within 48 hours and resolved within one month. Return, refund, exchange, warranty, delivery and payment-security information must be easy to find, and fake reviews are not allowed. Marketplace sellers must also provide details such as the total price breakdown and country of origin.

We build the pages, footers and product templates that display this information, and we keep review features limited to genuine customers. Your legal adviser should confirm exactly what applies to your business model, along with your duties under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
What Makes a Product Page Convert?

Product pages do most of the selling. When a Shopify developer and a designer plan them together, small details add up to more orders. We build product templates around the questions shoppers ask before they pay:

items: What exactly is this? Clear photos from several angles, a short video where useful, and a plain description written for buyers, not search engines.
Will it suit me? Size guides, compatibility notes, ingredients or specifications shown near the price.
When will it arrive? An estimated delivery date or range based on the shopper's pin code, where your courier data allows.
What if it is wrong? A short summary of the return and exchange policy, linked to the full page.
Can I trust this store? Genuine reviews from verified buyers, secure payment badges from your actual gateway and visible contact details.
What else do I need? Related products and bundles that genuinely help, not a wall of random suggestions.

main_content.text: We test these templates on real phones, because most Indian shoppers browse and buy on mobile, and we measure add-to-cart and checkout rates before and after changes.
How Do We Keep Your Store and Customer Data Secure?

Online stores hold names, addresses, phone numbers and order histories, so security is part of every build. On hosted platforms like Shopify, the platform secures the infrastructure and checkout, while your Shopify developer controls staff accounts, apps and integrations. On Magento and custom stores, hosting and updates are also our responsibility under a support plan.

items: Staff accounts with only the permissions each person needs, and two-step login for owners and admins.
Apps and extensions reviewed before installation, and removed when no longer used.
Regular platform, extension and theme updates, tested before they go live.
Payment data handled only by approved gateways, never stored in the store.
Backups of product and content data, and a written plan for what to do if something goes wrong.

main_content.text: Ecommerce Mobile App Development Company Services

Most stores should get the website right before building an app. An app makes sense when customers buy often, when push notifications and saved preferences add real value, or when loyalty features need a home on the phone. As an ecommerce mobile app development company, we build shopping apps that share products, carts, customers and orders with your Shopify or Magento store, so you manage everything in one place.
For Magento mobile app development, we connect the app to Magento's APIs, keeping prices, stock and customer groups in sync. Full details of our mobile work are on our app development page.
Marketing Your Store: A Digital Marketing Agency for Ecommerce

A new store does not sell on its own. Because we are also a digital marketing agency for ecommerce, the same team that builds your store can bring shoppers to it, and the store is built with marketing in mind from the start.

items: Ecommerce search engine optimization services: category and product page structure, unique product descriptions, product structured data, internal links and crawl control for filters.
Google Merchant Center feeds for free listings and Shopping ads.
Paid search and social campaigns measured on revenue and return on ad spend.
Email and WhatsApp flows for welcome, abandoned cart and repeat purchase, with customer consent.
Conversion work: product page tests, checkout friction fixes and trust signals based on real data.

main_content.text: What Does a Shopify Developer Check in a Store Audit?
Our free store audit is where most projects start. In it, a Shopify developer and a marketing specialist review the store the way a customer and a search engine see it.

items: Speed on a mid-range phone, and which apps or scripts slow the store down.
Product page clarity: photos, price, delivery promise, returns and trust details.
Collection and filter structure, and whether filtered pages create duplicate content.
Checkout steps, payment options, cash-on-delivery rules and error messages.
Installed apps: what each does, what it costs and whether it is still needed.
Legal pages, grievance officer details and policies required for Indian consumers.
Tracking: whether sales, add-to-cart and checkout events are recorded correctly.
Search visibility: titles, product structured data, indexing and Merchant Center status.

main_content.text: You receive a short written report with the issues ranked by impact and effort, so you can fix the quick wins yourself or ask us to handle them.
Store Speed and Core Web Vitals

Shoppers leave slow stores. We aim for Google's "good" Core Web Vitals thresholds on key templates: Largest Contentful Paint within 2.5 seconds, Interaction to Next Paint within 200 milliseconds and Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.1 or less, measured on real visits. In practice that means right-sized images, fewer apps, lazy-loaded media below the fold and theme code that loads only what each page needs.
How Does Our Ecommerce Development Process Work?
Every project follows the same stages, so nothing important is missed on the way to launch day, whether you need a full build or a Shopify developer for a defined task.

Before any move, we export products, customers and orders, map every old URL to its new home, test redirects, and plan the switch for a quiet sales period. Customer passwords usually cannot be moved between platforms, so we prepare a friendly email inviting customers to reset theirs. After launch, we watch orders, payment success rates and Search Console errors closely for the first weeks.

Monthly speed and conversion checks with suggested improvements.

Number of unique templates and the depth of custom design.

Integrations with ERP, accounting, warehouse, courier or marketing tools.

A clothing brand (details changed) takes orders through Instagram messages and bank transfers. Tracking sizes, payments and deliveries by hand is no longer possible. Situation 2: A Distributor Still on Magento 1

A hardware distributor (details changed) runs thousands of products on an old Magento 1 store with customer-specific pricing. Security patches stopped years ago. A skincare brand (details changed) has twenty-five apps installed, slow product pages and rising monthly app bills. Common Mistakes When Building an Online Store
These mistakes cost sales, money and time. Most are easy to avoid when planned early.

items: Choosing a platform because a friend uses it, without checking catalogue and integration needs.

items: Which platform do you recommend for my catalogue and order volume, and why?

items: Payment gateway: what documents do you need for approval, how long does it take and which payment methods are enabled for my business type?
Payment gateway: what are the settlement times and charges, and do you support saved-card tokens?

main_content.text: What This Service Does Not Do
To keep expectations clear, our ecommerce development service does not:

items: Guarantee a level of sales, conversion rate or Google ranking.
Store or handle customers' card numbers; payments go through approved gateways.
Write fake reviews or import reviews from other sites.

Hold your store, domain or data hostage. Everything is handed over.

We would rather tell you honestly when a full e-commerce project is not the right spend.

items: If you sell a handful of products and are still testing demand, a basic Shopify plan with a free theme may be enough to start.
If most of your sales come through marketplaces and you have no plan to drive your own traffic, improve your marketplace listings first.
If your current store converts well and only needs small fixes, ask for a support task rather than a rebuild.
If you cannot yet handle more orders, fix fulfilment before investing in a bigger store.

main_content.text: Special Cases and Edge Cases
Some stores need extra planning. We treat these separately.
Selling Internationally

Selling abroad means multiple currencies, international shipping, duties and country-specific rules. We set up markets, currencies and shipping zones, and ask you to confirm export and tax requirements with your advisers.
Subscriptions and Repeat Orders

Products like coffee, supplements or pet food suit subscriptions. Recurring payments in India have specific mandate rules handled by payment providers, so we choose a subscription tool and gateway combination that supports them.
Very Large Catalogues

Stores with tens of thousands of products need careful filters, search, feeds and crawl control. We plan category structure and filter indexing rules with SEO in mind, and import products with scripts and validation checks.
Regulated Products

Medicines, supplements, alcohol-related goods and some electronics carry extra rules on platforms, payment gateways and advertising. We ask you to confirm what you are allowed to sell online and how before we build product pages and checkout rules.
Multi-Vendor Marketplaces

If you want other sellers to list products on your site, you are building a marketplace, which brings extra rules and complex software. We plan these as custom builds with our custom web development team.

main_content.text: App Development Services vs Application Development Services

People use these phrases in different ways. Our app development services usually mean mobile apps installed from Google Play or the App Store. Application development services is a wider term that also covers web applications used in a browser. We do both, and many projects need both: a mobile app for customers and a web dashboard for staff. Web platforms are handled by our custom web development team, working alongside the app team.
Website and App Development Together

Many businesses need website and app development at the same time: a website that explains the service and ranks on search, and a mobile product that existing customers use every week. Planning them together means one login system, one product catalogue, one set of APIs and consistent branding. It also avoids paying two vendors to build the same back end twice.
Native, Cross-Platform or Web App: Which Should You Build?
The right technology depends on what the product must do, how fast you need it, your budget and who will maintain it. We recommend an approach after discovery and explain the trade-offs in writing.

rows: Native (Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS)

main_content.text: Cross-platform frameworks have matured a lot, and for most business apps they deliver a smooth experience at a lower total cost than two native apps. We do not claim they are identical to native in every case; when a feature needs native code, we write that part natively and connect it.
Flutter App Development Company

As a Flutter app development company, we use Flutter when you want a distinctive design that looks the same on Android and iPhone, smooth custom animations, or one team maintaining both platforms. Flutter also suits apps that may later run on tablets or the web from the same code.
React Native App Development Company

As a React Native app development company, we choose React Native when your product already has a React website, when your in-house team knows JavaScript, or when you want to reuse business logic across web and mobile. It renders real platform components, so lists, inputs and navigation feel native on each system.
Native App Development Services, iOS App Development and Android Apps

Our native app development services suit products that rely heavily on the camera, Bluetooth devices, sensors, background location, audio processing or platform features such as widgets. For iOS app development we use Swift and Apple's tools; for Android we use Kotlin. As an Android app development company, we also plan for the very wide range of Android devices in India, from budget phones with limited memory to flagship models, and our Android application development services include testing on older Android versions your customers still use.
Custom Mobile App Development vs App Builders

Builders and white-label templates can launch something basic quickly. They work for simple catalogues or content apps. Custom mobile app development makes sense when your workflow, pricing, logistics or user experience is what makes your business different, when you need to own the code, or when monthly builder fees and limits start to cost more than a build. We will tell you honestly if a builder is enough for your stage.

main_content.text: What Are the Google Play and App Store Requirements in 2026?
Store rules change every year, and missing one can block a launch or an update. These are some current requirements we plan for. We re-check the official pages before every submission.

rows: New apps and app updates must target Android 16 (API level 36) or higher
From 31 August 2026; developers can request an extension to 1 November 2026
New personal developer accounts must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 consecutive days before applying for production access
Applies to personal accounts created after 13 November 2023
Uploads to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later, using the iOS 26 SDK or newer
Privacy disclosures: Google Play's Data safety form and Apple's App Privacy details must match what the app actually collects
Checked at review and when data use changes

main_content.text: No developer can guarantee that Apple or Google will approve a submission on the first try, because reviews depend on the stores' own policies and reviewers. What we can do is follow the published guidelines, prepare complete test accounts and notes for reviewers, and respond quickly to any questions.
Personal or Organisation Developer Account?

Food Delivery App Development Company

Live tracking, slot-based delivery, ratings from real customers and payment integration are standard building blocks. Grocery Delivery App Development Company

Payments, lending, insurance and investment apps are regulated. main_content.text: What Sits Behind the App: Back End, Admin Panel and Integrations
Most of the work in a serious mobile product is invisible to users. Everything we build comes with:

items: A secure API that the phone talks to, documented for future developers.
An admin panel to manage users, content, orders, prices and reports without a developer.
Push notifications that users can control, with sensible limits so they are not annoying.
Analytics events for the actions that matter, such as sign-ups, orders and repeat use.
Crash and error reporting, so problems are found before users complain.
Integrations with payment gateways, maps, messaging, CRM or ERP systems where they offer APIs.

main_content.text: How Do We Keep Your App Secure and Private?
Phones get lost, networks are public and apps hold personal data, so security is part of the design.

items: Login with OTP, email or social sign-in, and optional biometric unlock using the phone's own secure features.
Sensitive data stored in the platform's secure storage, never in plain text on the device.
All traffic encrypted; servers check permissions on every request, not just the app screen.
Only the device permissions the product truly needs, requested at the moment they are useful.
Payment card data handled only by approved payment gateways.
Privacy policy, Data safety and App Privacy disclosures that match what it actually does.

main_content.text: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 are coming into force in phases. We can build consent screens, data-deletion requests and access controls, but your legal adviser should confirm what your product must do.
Designing for Everyone: Accessibility and Inclusive Design

A mobile product should work for people with low vision, limited dexterity, hearing loss or little experience with smartphones. Inclusive design also helps everyone else, for example when someone is using a phone in bright sunlight or with one hand on a crowded bus. We follow the accessibility guidance built into Android and iOS and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines where they apply to mobile screens.

items: Text that respects the phone's font-size setting and still fits the layout.
Colour contrast that stays readable outdoors, and meaning never shown by colour alone.
Touch targets large enough for thumbs, with enough space between them.
Labels for screen readers such as TalkBack and VoiceOver on every button and image that matters.
Captions or transcripts for video lessons and spoken content.
Simple language, clear error messages and the option to go back without losing work.

main_content.text: We check these points during design reviews and test key journeys with screen readers before release. Building them in from the start costs far less than fixing them after launch, and it widens the audience your product can reach.
Launch Is the Start: Updates, OS Changes and Support

Android and iOS release major versions every year, devices change and stores update their rules, as the 2026 requirements above show. Software that is never updated slowly breaks or gets removed from the stores. Our optional support covers bug fixes, updates for new OS versions and store requirements, dependency and security updates, crash monitoring, performance checks and small improvements. New features are planned and quoted as phases. You can end support at any time and receive a full handover.

We do not publish fixed prices on this page, because two projects that sound similar can need very different work. The total is made up of a few clear parts:

items: Number of apps (for example customer, partner and admin) and user roles.
Number of screens and the complexity of features such as live tracking, chat or offline mode.
Technology approach: cross-platform, native or a mix.
Back end and admin panel scope, and integrations with other systems.
Design depth, from a clean standard interface to a fully custom design system.
Third-party costs paid directly to providers: developer accounts, maps, SMS, cloud hosting, video or payment services.
Testing range, security reviews and ongoing support after launch.

These situations are illustrative. They are based on common requests; names and details are changed, and they are not client case studies or promised results.
Situation 1: A Restaurant Group Paying High Commissions

A restaurant group (details changed) gets most delivery orders through large aggregators and wants a direct channel for loyal customers. We would build a branded ordering app with saved addresses, repeat orders, loyalty points and a kitchen display panel, connected to their own delivery staff and payment gateway, while they continue on aggregators for new customers.
Situation 2: A Coaching Institute Moving Classes Online

A coaching institute (details changed) runs classes through video links shared on WhatsApp and tracks fees in spreadsheets. We would build a learning app with recorded lectures, live-class links, tests, progress reports and fee reminders, with parent accounts and consent flows for students under 18.
Situation 3: A Field-Service Company Still Using Paper Job Cards

An appliance-repair company (details changed) sends technicians out with paper job cards, so updates and payments are slow. We would build a technician app that works offline, captures photos and customer signatures, collects payments by UPI and syncs to a web dashboard for the office team.
Common Mistakes in App Projects
These mistakes cost money, months and user trust. Most are easy to avoid when planned early.

items: Trying to launch every feature at once instead of a focused first version.
Building an app when a mobile-friendly website would serve customers better.
Registering developer accounts in the agency's or a freelancer's name.
Testing only on the latest flagship phones, not on the budget devices many users own.
Ignoring the admin panel, so staff cannot manage the app without a developer.
Asking for every phone permission on first launch, which makes users uninstall.
Forgetting store privacy forms and policies until the week of submission.
Leaving no budget for updates after launch, so the app falls behind OS and store requirements.
Copying a large competitor's app feature for feature without a clear reason for users to switch.

Ask any team of app developers these questions, including us. Clear written answers are a good sign.

items: Which technology do you recommend for my app, and why that one?
Will the code, designs and both store accounts be in my company's name?

What does the admin panel include, and can my team use it without help?

What support do you offer after launch, and how quickly do you fix crashes?

Some answers sit with your providers. Before the project starts, check:

items: Apple and Google: which account type suits your business, what documents are needed and how long verification takes.

To keep expectations clear, our app development service does not:

items: Guarantee approval by Apple or Google, a store ranking or a number of downloads.
Publish apps under our own developer accounts on your behalf.
Copy another company's app design, brand or content.
Use cracked or unlicensed libraries, tools or assets.
Run regulated activities such as lending, payments or insurance; those require licensed partners.

main_content.text: When You Do Not Need an App
We would rather save you money than build something nobody installs.

items: If customers interact with you only a few times a year, a fast mobile website is usually better.
If you are still testing demand, a progressive web app or a no-code prototype can prove the idea first.
If an existing app or marketplace already serves your customers well, improve your listing there first.
If there is no budget to maintain the app after launch, wait until there is.

main_content.text: Special Cases and Edge Cases
Some apps need extra planning. We treat these separately.
Offline-First Apps

Field staff, drivers and rural users often lose network. We store data safely on the device, let users keep working and sync changes automatically when the connection returns, with clear signs of what has and has not synced.
Budget Phones and Small Storage
Many users in India have phones with limited memory and storage. We keep app size down, compress images, avoid heavy background tasks and test on low-end devices before release.
Indian Languages
Apps in Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and other languages need careful fonts, layouts that handle longer words and content managed from the admin panel without app updates.
Taking Over an Existing App

If your previous developer has left, we audit the code, accounts, build set-up and store listings before suggesting whether to continue, refactor or rebuild. We also check that the store accounts and signing keys are under your control.
Apps for Children
Apps aimed at children face stricter store policies and data rules. We plan age-appropriate design, parental consent and minimal data collection from the first workshop.

What Makes Users Keep Using an App?
Downloads are easy to buy and easy to lose. Retention, meaning how many people come back next week and next month, decides whether a mobile product succeeds. We design for it from the start:

items: A first session that delivers value within a minute, without long sign-up forms.

main_content.text: Get Found on Google and AI Search With a Transparent SEO Agency
Technical, local, content and e-commerce SEO from one team in Bengaluru, built on Google's own guidelines.

SEO (search engine optimisation) is the work of making a website easier for search engines to crawl, understand and trust, so it appears when your customers search. An SEO agency plans and carries out that work. Afwan Tech is an SEO agency in Whitefield, Bengaluru offering local, organic, e-commerce and SaaS SEO, with technical fixes made by our own developers.

Good search optimisation is slow, steady and measurable, and a good SEO agency shows its work. It means fixing what stops search engines reading your site, publishing pages that answer real questions better than competitors do, earning genuine mentions and links, and keeping your business details accurate everywhere. We do that work in the open: a written plan, a shared task list and reports that track enquiries and sales, not just rankings. We never promise a guaranteed position, because nobody outside Google can honestly do that.
